source.label: CDC — About Heat and Your Health

consequences.detail: Hot days dry your body out faster.
You can feel faint when you stand up.
Your heart pumps more to cool you down.
Some medicines change your blood salts in heat.
A warning sign that your body is too hot.

stay_cool.detail: Use AC at home, or go to a cool public place such as a library.
If you are outside, take breaks and keep out of the sun.
Do outdoor things early in the morning or in the evening.
Above 90°F a fan can make your body hotter, not cooler.

stay_hydrated.detail: Drink and refill it through the day.
Also limit very sugary or salty drinks and caffeine.
Light yellow or clear usually means you are drinking enough.

medicines.detail: Never stop or change them without talking to your doctor.

medicines.phrase: Store them out of the heat
medicines.detail: Some medicines must be kept cool.
Know what to do about fridge medicines and electrical devices.

check_ins.detail: Call family, friends and neighbours, especially anyone who lives alone.

emergency.detail: If you feel confused, faint, or very weak, this is an emergency.

disclaimer: This is a hackathon demo, not medical advice. Do not stop or change any medicine without talking to your care team.
